title: graph.json is written non-atomically and read with no corrupt-file handling, while concurrent readers exist
scenario: save() writes graph.json in place (depgraph.py:57-60) - the only multi-writer state file in the codebase NOT using the tmp+os.replace pattern that loop.save, kb._atomic_json and _meter_bump all use. load() (depgraph.py:50-53) does a bare json.load. In a parallel wave, one worker's evaluate triggers depgraph.scan(ws) (loop.py:686) while another gate/brief concurrently calls depgraph.load via impact()/_submission_staleness; a read landing mid-write raises raw JSONDecodeError and the gate/evaluate step dies with a traceback. Concurrent scan() + record_edge() also do unserialized load->save, so a recorded edge can be silently lost.
fix: Make depgraph.save atomic (tmp + os.replace, same as loop.save) and serialize scan/record_edge/link_requirement read-modify-writes under a graph.json.lock flock like loop.mutate; make load() treat a corrupt file as a structured error instead of a bare traceback.

title: Graph-DoR refusal 'new/unknown graph modules were not declared' never names the new_modules field
scenario: Plan gate in /tmp/qa2-serial with a task whose scope adds tests/**: blocker 'task t1: new/unknown graph modules were not declared: tests'. The remedy — adding "new_modules": ["tests"] to the task in plan/tasks.json (read at depgraph.py:791) — appears nowhere in the message, the plan-step instruction, or `loop next` output; a planner can only discover it by reading source.
fix: Append the mechanism to the error: 'declare them in the task's "new_modules" list in plan/tasks.json'.

title: Graph scan walks the whole tree at every gate and SKIP_DIRS misses vendored/build trees (and ignores .gitignore)
scenario: scan() os.walks the entire workspace (line 353) at every serial evaluate (loop.py:686), plan readiness (depgraph.readiness:771), signoff (_signoff_dod:1713) and EM true-up. SKIP_DIRS covers node_modules/venv/dist/build but not vendor/ (Go), target/ (Rust/Java), .next/, coverage/, .terraform/, Pods/, and it never consults .gitignore. On a Go repo with vendor/ or a Java repo with an unwiped target/, thousands of third-party files are read, hashed and turned into modules: graph.json balloons to tens of MB, every module_of/ext: edge from vendored code pollutes impact() blast radius (reviewers get hundreds of false 'impacted' modules), and each gate pays a full-tree walk + stat of ~100k files even with the mtime short-circuit.
fix: Enumerate candidate files via `git ls-files` (the module already shells to git everywhere) with the os.walk as fallback for non-repo dirs — that inherits .gitignore for free; at minimum extend SKIP_DIRS with vendor, target, .next, coverage, .terraform, Pods, out.

title: graph.json is fully re-read on every load() and fully rewritten on every recorded edge — O(graph) I/O multiplied per gate
scenario: load() parses the whole graph.json — including the per-file {hash, imports, size, mtime} cache, by far its largest section — with no memoization. One `loop next` at evaluate/em calls load() at least 4-6 times (impact, product_impact, summary, hub_signal via lens routing, _design_context). On a 10k-file repo the file is several MB, so each transition pays 10-30 full JSON parses across the call graph. Writes are worse at the plan gate: _annotate_plan_graph calls link_requirement per requirement and record_edge per contract, and each of those does load→mutate→_stamp_meta (which re-serializes ALL file hashes to compute the fingerprint)→save of the entire file — a 20-task plan with contracts does ~30 full-file rewrite cycles.
fix: Add a module-level memo in load() keyed on (path, mtime, size) invalidated by save(), and split the file cache from the module/edge graph (two files: graph.json + graph-files.json) so edge recording and impact queries stop paying for the file cache; batch _annotate_plan_graph's edge writes into one load→N mutations→one save.

title: Go scanner silently produces external-only edges - blast radius for Go repos is near-empty, limitation unnamed
scenario: The Go branch (depgraph.py:436-441) turns EVERY import into `ext:<last-segment>` - internal package imports are never resolved to modules, unlike Python (known_stems), JS (file index), C#/Java (namespace maps) and Ruby (which even carries an honest comment about Rails autoloading at _ruby_imports:292-294). A Go monorepo therefore gets a graph with no internal edges: impact() returns ~zero dependents, hub_signal never escalates architecture review, and graph DoD passes trivially - while README sells 'dependency-aware execution and review' host-agnostically. The asymmetry is a real scope cut, but it is recorded nowhere: no code comment, no doc caveat, no revisit trigger.
fix: Smallest fix is honesty: a comment at the Go branch mirroring the Ruby note ('internal Go imports are not resolved - record intra-repo edges with tp graph edge'), plus a line in the graph docs. Better: resolve imports whose path starts with the module path from go.mod (one regex read) so internal edges land like the other six languages.

title: Single monolithic index.json grows without bound and ids are dense len+1 — no archival, and deletion would break id minting
scenario: Every decision, flow, requirement, and debt item appends to one index.json forever; list/retrieve load the whole file on every call (kb.py:36-41), and private-store ids are minted as len(idx['decisions'])+1 (kb.py:122) so any future compaction/removal of superseded entries would re-mint an existing id. At thousands of entries every `tp context` SessionStart hook pays the full parse cost.
fix: Mint ids from a monotonic counter stored in the index (not len()), and add a compaction path that archives superseded/done entries to index-archive.json so the hot index stays small.

title: kb.lint re-reads the entire knowledge store on every DoD/signoff, and the store only ever grows
scenario: lint() os.walks tp.kb_root(ws) plus plan/ and specs/ and reads every .md/.json file fully, scanning for markers. It runs at every `tp dod` (tp.py:710) and inside _signoff_dod (loop.py:1730) — which ALSO reruns every task's test suite serially. Decisions, requirements, debt and flows accumulate across all tracks with no archival, so a project with a few hundred tracks has thousands of files: each signoff re-reads all of them, and the signoff gate's latency grows linearly with total project history rather than with the track being signed off.
fix: Lint incrementally: keep a lint-state file mapping path→(mtime,size,verdict) in the store and re-scan only new/changed files (same mtime+size short-circuit depgraph.scan already uses); full rescan stays available behind `tp kb lint --all`.

title: hub_signal and _edge_nudges swallow all exceptions with no trace - a broken graph silently degrades routing
scenario: lens.hub_signal wraps its whole body in `except Exception: return 0` (lens.py:104-118) and loop._edge_nudges in `except Exception: pass` (loop.py:337-338), with no trace() event. If graph.json is corrupt or an edge row is malformed, the hub escalation (architecture full-pass on hub modules) and the runtime-edge nudges just stop firing forever, and nothing in trace.jsonl or any dashboard shows the degradation - unlike the sibling fail-opens (_with_dashboard is commented; graph_refresh_failed IS traced at loop.py:683/691).
fix: Keep the fail-open but emit tp.trace(ws, 'hub_signal_failed'/'edge_nudge_failed', error=str(exc)) so the degradation is visible in the audit trail, matching the graph_refresh_failed pattern.

title: _HARD_LENSES names a nonexistent 'concurrency' lens — the deep-tier cost map drifts from the catalog unchecked
scenario: lenses/catalog.json has 26 lenses and none is 'concurrency', yet _HARD_LENSES includes it (lens.py:28-29). The entry is dead: whatever review the deep-tier budget was meant to buy for concurrency reasoning never happens, and nothing asserts the tier map stays a subset of the catalog, so future renames silently downgrade a hard lens from the deep model to standard — a quiet quality/cost misallocation.
fix: Remove 'concurrency' (or add the lens) and add a one-line test asserting _HARD_LENSES <= {lens ids in catalog.json}.
